items.title: When the Grimms began publishing
items.claim: The first edition of the Brothers Grimm's Kinder- und Hausmarchen appeared in which year?
items.reveal:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected tales partly from middle-class informants of Huguenot background, including Dorothea Viehmann.

Later editions softened violence in some tales. Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project was completed only in 1961.
items.why: The 'folk' in folklore is often more bourgeois and literate than the framing implies.

items.title: Klemperer's LTI
items.claim: Victor Klemperer's LTI: Notizbuch eines Philologen (1947) studied which subject?

options.text: The language of the Third Reich, observed during the war by a Romance philologist who survived persecution

items.reveal_title: A close linguistic analysis of Nazi-era German
items.reveal:
Klemperer (Romanist at Dresden, dismissed in 1935) compiled a study of Nazi-period vocabulary, rhetoric and propaganda forms.

The book has remained continuously in print as a model of linguistic study under dictatorship.
items.why: Documentary records of how a regime uses language can outlast the regime itself.

items.title: 1996 spelling reform
items.claim: A German spelling reform was agreed in 1996 and implemented in stages. Which change is genuinely part of it?

options.text: Abolition of capital letters on nouns
Replacing ß with ss after short vowels in many words (e.g. dass instead of daß)

items.reveal:
The reform rationalised ss usage according to vowel length, modified some compound spellings and changed comma rules.

Major newspapers reversed and re-adopted parts of the reform in the early 2000s, settling on a revised version by 2006.
items.why: Orthographic reforms often face strong public reaction and partial reversal.
